correctness.rationale: Column products decouple. For inputs (t,b) and (s,c), the witness equations are (t-s)u=0, (1-s)z=c-bu and (t-s)v=0, (1-t)w=b-cv. When neither scalar is 1, take u=v=0 and solve by division. When both are 1, the equations require reciprocal scalar multiples, equivalent to equal nonzero lines or two zero vectors. In the mixed case the diagonal-1 vector must vanish, which is also sufficient. All choices assemble into allowed witnesses. Thus the one-column star and line fibers have sizes 1+(q-1)q^d and q-1 respectively; line count is (q^d-1)/(q-1), and products give every class multiplicity. Squaring yields precisely t=0 with arbitrary b or (t,b)=(1,0) as idempotents. For q=2 this equals the star fiber; over any larger field diag(I,aI) for a not 0 or 1 disproves equality. As a bounded cross-check from actual block multiplication, K_{1,1} over F_3 has a seven-element star class (six t≠1 plus the identity) and one two-element class, with four idempotents. The counterexample X(0,2) and the identity are mutually intertwined by X(0,0). This check is additional to the universal algebraic argument; uploaded code was inspected but not executed.
residual_risks: No formal verification claimed; the bounded reproduction does not exhaust arbitrary graphs or fields.

value.rationale: The open problem asks for more than idempotents being mutually conjugate: the result identifies their full containing class, produces a counterexample over the original complex base, distinguishes the F_2 exception, and gives a uniform classification with class sizes for noncomplete as well as complete bipartite graphs. Dependence on the witness monoid makes this useful beyond a conjugacy calculation by units.
residual_risks: Does not answer the questions about primary, norm or trace conjugacy, or the analogous classification for other antichains.
